title: JMoney's Rookie Solo: One Win, Seven Pickups, and a Season Still Playing On
body: Jordan arrived in the Buckaroo Football League in 2026, part of the expansion class that took the league from six teams to eight, and he showed up with a team name that is already a conversation starter: Counting or not Counting GV. The early returns have been rough. Through seven weeks, JMoney sits at 1-6 with 622.5 points for, roughly 89 a week. That isn't a disaster on paper, but it has been a disaster on the scoreboard.

The lone win is the one everyone will remember. In week 5, Counting or not Counting GV dropped a season-best 119.7 on Zoe's Ghostu-Spider SZN, the best performance of Jordan's young career and the only game where the band actually hit every note. The other end came in week 7, when Ramon's No Banner only HULK held him to 60.9, his worst output to date. Losing to the best team in the league is no shame, but losing to Brucie by that kind of margin lingers.

The head-to-head ledger reads like a tour where every stop booed: 0-1 against Randy, Sonny, Alan, Mekhi, Kaushal and Ramon, and 1-0 against Zoe. That makes Z² the only manager JMoney can claim to own, and the only rivalry where he holds the bragging rights. Everyone else has a receipt on him, and Philly in particular is not the type to let anyone forget it.

As a manager, Jordan hasn't been sitting still. He has made seven pickups and one trade, which is more activity than you'd expect from a 1-6 team and suggests he's still tuning the lineup rather than packing up the instruments. Whether those moves turn into wins is the open question for the back half of the schedule.

Here's where he stands: the title odds read 0%, the playoff seed is blank, and the season is still in progress. That leaves JMoney playing for pride, for spoiler duty, and for a better showing on the consolation ladder. Every great career has a rough first movement, and Jordan still has time to write a better second one.
